I am having so much fun with these science posters. They are great for visualizing the news on X and other platforms. 

4 images, 4:5, 4 scientific news that were in the news : class Retro_Editorial_Poster:     def __init__(self, topic="[$TOPIC]", org="[$ORGANIZATION]"):         self.canvas = "Aged, slightly worn vintage poster paper with halftone dot printing artifacts."         self.layout = "Asymmetrical Swiss Grid: Left text rail, top hero image, bottom data panels, bottom right contextual photo."      def semantic_asset_generation(self):         # AI AUTO-INFERENCE: Generate specific visuals based on the topic         hero_image = infer_hero_visual(self.topic) # e.g., A galaxy, a microchip, a deep-sea creature         context_photo = infer_exhibition_context(self.topic) # e.g., Silhouettes of people looking at a screen         data_thumbnails = infer_technical_details(self.topic, count=3) # e.g., 3 small B&W radar/x-ray shots         return [hero_image, context_photo, data_thumbnails]      def typography_and_ui(self):         # Establish the text hierarchy         sidebar = f"Massive vertical black text on cream background reading '{self.topic.upper()}'."         main_title = f"Bold halftone/stipple font reading '{self.topic.upper()}' with orange sub-text."         logos = f"Bottom left features the {self. org} logo and clean sans-serif exhibition details."         return [sidebar, main_title, logos]  render_poster_layout(Retro_Editorial_Poster())
